title: Atlas Multiplication Registry
purpose: A living expansion engine for moving file by file through the Atlas and multiplying useful information by coupling compatible records, evidence, measurements, timelines and relationships rather than creating disconnected lists.
method: find empirical or textual evidence where appropriate
route the result through the graph
epistemic_rule: Coupling means a meaningful relationship, analogy or comparison. It does not by itself prove causation, historical influence, physical identity or divine intent.
multiplication_formula: one record × definitions × attributes × chronology × geography × evidence × relationships × comparisons × measurements × events × dependencies × routes = many useful retrieval paths

coupling_families.name: Potato–vesica
coupling_families.why: The project treats the potato as the coupled overlap of distinguishable poles.

coupling_families.name: Potato–eye–sprout
coupling_families.why: A potato eye is a bud capable of initiating new growth.

coupling_families.name: Potato–root–memory
coupling_families.why: The buried side of the potato provides a natural metaphor for stored history, ancestry and material continuity.

coupling_families.name: Potato–seed–future
coupling_families.why: Dormant plant material can retain capacity for renewed growth.

coupling_families.name: Potato–thalamus
coupling_families.why: The project compares a central container with differentiated interior regions and outward pathways.

coupling_families.name: Nucleus–room
coupling_families.why: A nucleus is a functional neural region; a room is a functional architectural region.

coupling_families.name: Axon–road
coupling_families.why: Each is a route through which something moves between regions, although the transported entities differ.

coupling_families.name: Eye–LGN–cortex
coupling_families.why: Visual information travels through a defined thalamic relay architecture.

coupling_families.name: Gate–attention
coupling_families.why: Access and processing are both selective rather than unlimited.

coupling_families.name: House–rooms–roads
coupling_families.why: Container, internal differentiation and connection form a common systems grammar.

coupling_families.name: Father–House
coupling_families.why: The Father's House is the project's spatial metaphor for source and dwelling.

coupling_families.name: House–John 14
coupling_families.why: John 14 supplies the canonical Christian house/rooms vocabulary used by the project.

coupling_families.name: Son–Door
coupling_families.why: The Son is modeled as the threshold through which the inner and outer domains communicate.

coupling_families.name: Door–Matthew 7
coupling_families.why: The narrow gate is a direct biblical threshold motif.

coupling_families.name: Door–John 10
coupling_families.why: John 10 provides explicit door/gate language in relation to Jesus.

coupling_families.name: Door–wedge
coupling_families.why: A wedge can model narrowing toward a passage; the project's Door is a concentrated threshold.

coupling_families.name: Wedge–vesica
coupling_families.why: The pointed ends of a lens create a natural visual vocabulary for narrowing and emergence.

coupling_families.name: Tree–Potato
coupling_families.why: The project treats the tree as the unfolded architecture of what is latent in the potato.

coupling_families.name: Tree–root–fruit
coupling_families.why: Plant morphology links hidden support to visible reproductive output.

coupling_families.name: Tree–brain
coupling_families.why: Branching is a common topology, not an identity between plant and brain.

coupling_families.name: Tree–network
coupling_families.why: Trees are a formal graph class and also a biological branching form.

coupling_families.name: Vine–branches
coupling_families.why: John 15 explicitly uses plant branching and fruitfulness as relational imagery.

coupling_families.name: Tree–Genesis
coupling_families.why: Genesis places two named trees inside a garden narrative.

coupling_families.name: Knowledge–differentiation
coupling_families.why: The project reads knowledge partly as differentiation and distinction; this is interpretation, not a claim about authorial intent.

coupling_families.name: Life–death–seed
coupling_families.why: Organic systems cycle through growth, senescence, decomposition and renewed potential.

coupling_families.name: Ash–memory
coupling_families.why: Ash can function as a material trace of what has been transformed or consumed.

coupling_families.name: Mud–soil–root
coupling_families.why: The project's mud imagery can be coupled to the literal soil environment of tuber growth.

coupling_families.name: Swamp–drain
coupling_families.why: A drainage problem can represent blocked or polluted system flow while remaining a metaphor when applied socially.

coupling_families.name: Drain–negative-flow
coupling_families.why: Flows can leave a system without generating replenishment.

coupling_families.name: Repair–Tikun
coupling_families.why: Tikun Olam provides a comparative vocabulary for repair without being equated with Potatoism.

coupling_families.name: Look–attention
coupling_families.why: The project makes attention a prerequisite for intervention.

coupling_families.name: Evidence–witness
coupling_families.why: Evidence allows a claim to be checked against something external to the claimant.

coupling_families.name: Unknown–not-zero
coupling_families.why: Absence of observation must not silently become a measurement of zero.

coupling_families.name: Record–node
coupling_families.why: Every substantive record should have a stable identity and a route into the graph.

coupling_families.name: Node–edge
coupling_families.why: The Atlas is relationship-first: isolated descriptions lose context.

coupling_families.name: Edge–trajectory
coupling_families.why: Relationships can change strength, direction, status and meaning over time.

coupling_families.name: Topology–trajectory
coupling_families.why: A graph needs both structure and change to explain evolving systems.

coupling_families.name: Feedback–spiral
coupling_families.why: Repeated feedback can amplify, dampen or redirect a trajectory.

coupling_families.name: Red–Blue
coupling_families.why: The project uses Red and Blue as complementary tendencies within one Potato.

coupling_families.name: Expansion–contraction
coupling_families.why: Systems often trade exploration against retention and stability.

coupling_families.name: Love–fear
coupling_families.why: The project's polarity can be used as a vocabulary for approach versus avoidance, without reducing human emotion to one axis.

coupling_families.name: Knowledge–ignorance
coupling_families.why: Every map creates known regions and exposes unknown ones.

coupling_families.name: North–orientation
coupling_families.why: North can be treated as geographic orientation and separately as project symbolism.

coupling_families.name: Mountain–axis
coupling_families.why: Mountains commonly provide elevated orientation points in myths and geography.

coupling_families.name: Ladder–Jacob
coupling_families.why: Genesis 28 supplies the canonical ladder/ascending-descending image.

coupling_families.name: Ladder–Son
coupling_families.why: John 1:51 connects ascending/descending imagery to the Son of Man.

coupling_families.name: Stone–House
coupling_families.why: Jacob's Bethel narrative provides a place, stone and house-of-God cluster.

coupling_families.name: Stone–potato
coupling_families.why: Both can serve as grounded material objects in the project's earth/threshold vocabulary; not a historical equivalence.

coupling_families.name: Vessel–body
coupling_families.why: Vessel language makes embodiment a container/interface problem.

coupling_families.name: Body–city
coupling_families.why: Both can be modeled as differentiated subsystems coupled by transport and communication.

coupling_families.name: City–brain
coupling_families.why: Urban networks and neural networks both involve hubs, routes and distributed activity, while their physical mechanisms differ.

coupling_families.name: City–tree
coupling_families.why: Transport networks can branch like trees while also forming loops absent from a pure tree graph.

coupling_families.name: Economy–circulation
coupling_families.why: Economic systems depend on flows of goods, money, credit and information.

coupling_families.name: Debt–obligation
coupling_families.why: Debt is a recorded obligation connecting present action to future settlement.

coupling_families.name: Bank–memory
coupling_families.why: Ledgers preserve claims across time; Potato Bank is a project metaphor for stored value/obligation.

coupling_families.name: Ledger–archive
coupling_families.why: Both preserve structured historical state for later verification.

coupling_families.name: Audit–attention
coupling_families.why: Audit is institutionalized careful looking.

coupling_families.name: Integrity–repair
coupling_families.why: A graph is trustworthy only when references and content remain coherent.

coupling_families.name: Frontend–interface
coupling_families.why: The frontend is the user's Door into the repository.

coupling_families.name: Node page–Door
coupling_families.why: A node page should expose both the entity and the pathways around it.

coupling_families.name: Index–map
coupling_families.why: The front page should orient the reader before asking them to inspect detail.

coupling_families.name: Search–attention
coupling_families.why: Search is directed attention over a corpus.

coupling_families.name: Country–system
coupling_families.why: A country record becomes substantially more useful when coupled to its major systems.

coupling_families.name: Country–energy
coupling_families.why: Energy dependence creates observable cross-border relationships.

coupling_families.name: Country–trade
coupling_families.why: Trade links countries through flows rather than isolated statistics.

coupling_families.name: Country–population
coupling_families.why: Population becomes analytically useful when connected to labour, ageing, migration and fiscal systems.

coupling_families.name: Population–infrastructure
coupling_families.why: People require physical and institutional capacity to live and work.

coupling_families.name: Population–belief
coupling_families.why: Belief traditions have geographic, demographic and institutional footprints that can be researched without stereotyping populations.

coupling_families.name: Religion–text
coupling_families.why: Traditions can be mapped through texts, practices, institutions and historical change.

coupling_families.name: Religion–symbol
coupling_families.why: Recurring symbols can be compared while preserving tradition-specific meanings.

coupling_families.name: Bible–brain
coupling_families.why: The Atlas can compare textual metaphors with neuroanatomical structures without claiming biblical authors knew modern anatomy.

coupling_families.name: Bible–geometry
coupling_families.why: Geometric forms can be used as later interpretive lenses for biblical imagery.

coupling_families.name: Ancient-eye–modern-eye
coupling_families.why: Eye motifs recur, but recurrence alone does not establish historical transmission.

coupling_families.name: World-tree–tree-of-life
coupling_families.why: Both provide useful comparison around vertical world-structure while remaining distinct traditions.

coupling_families.name: Myth–geography
coupling_families.why: Physical landscapes are frequently transformed into symbolic spaces in myth.

coupling_families.name: North–Arctic
coupling_families.why: The project has both literal northern geography and symbolic North vocabulary.

coupling_families.name: North Programme–graph
coupling_families.why: The programme is represented as a network of observable economic relationships rather than a static list of countries.

coupling_families.name: Energy–infrastructure
coupling_families.why: Energy is physically constrained by infrastructure capacity and topology.

coupling_families.name: Technology–energy
coupling_families.why: Digital and advanced industrial systems depend on physical energy and infrastructure.

coupling_families.name: Technology–minerals
coupling_families.why: Advanced technologies depend on material supply chains.

coupling_families.name: Infrastructure–security
coupling_families.why: Critical infrastructure creates security dependencies and requires redundancy.

coupling_families.name: Security–law
coupling_families.why: Security functions are bounded by legal authorities and oversight structures.

coupling_families.name: Extremism–classification
coupling_families.why: Classification varies by jurisdiction and time and must remain source-specific.

coupling_families.name: Event–network
coupling_families.why: Events can be modeled as transformations of relationships, not just dates.

coupling_families.name: History–trajectory
coupling_families.why: History is a sequence of changing states and relationships.

coupling_families.name: Turning–threshold
coupling_families.why: The April 2025 material already models turning as a threshold event.

coupling_families.name: Crucifixion–transformation
coupling_families.why: Within project canon, the crucifixion event is a transformation of role and state.

coupling_families.name: Death–decomposition
coupling_families.why: Biological decomposition redistributes material rather than simply erasing it.

coupling_families.name: Christmas–birth
coupling_families.why: Christmas is part of the project's North/Christ transformation chronology.

coupling_families.name: Thomas–Twin
coupling_families.why: Thomas's name and later traditions create a strong twin/recognition vocabulary.

coupling_families.name: Twin–mirror
coupling_families.why: Twin and mirror both create identity through relation to a similar other.

coupling_families.name: Lion–courage
coupling_families.why: Lion imagery can carry kingship, courage and protection motifs in the project.

coupling_families.name: Service–kingship
coupling_families.why: The project distinguishes symbolic kingship from political authority and emphasizes stewardship.

coupling_families.name: Potato–Atlas
coupling_families.why: The Atlas itself becomes a digital Potato: a container whose value comes from internal connections and pathways.

coupling_families.name: Repository–memory
coupling_families.why: Version control preserves successive states of the project.

coupling_families.name: Commit–seed
coupling_families.why: A commit records a state that can generate future branches and revisions.

coupling_families.name: Branch–tree
coupling_families.why: Software branches and biological branches share a useful branching metaphor while operating differently.

coupling_families.name: Merge–vesica
coupling_families.why: A merge combines distinct histories into a new state; the vesica models overlap, not identical mechanics.

coupling_families.name: Fork–differentiation
coupling_families.why: A fork preserves common ancestry while creating divergent paths.

coupling_families.name: Research–growth
coupling_families.why: Research should create verified structure, not merely more text.

coupling_families.name: Question–edge
coupling_families.why: A good question often identifies a missing edge or unresolved node.

coupling_families.name: Hypothesis–evidence
coupling_families.why: Interpretations become stronger when exposed to evidence and possible disconfirmation.

coupling_families.name: Pattern–invariant
coupling_families.why: A pattern is most useful when the same relation survives translation without pretending the objects are identical.

coupling_families.name: Analogy–boundary
coupling_families.why: Every analogy needs an explicit boundary around what it does and does not establish.

coupling_families.name: Symbol–measurement
coupling_families.why: Where a symbolic claim contains mathematical structure, the measurable part should be separated from interpretation.

coupling_families.name: Geometry–architecture
coupling_families.why: The vesica and related constructions have documented roles in geometric construction and later architectural/artistic use.

coupling_families.name: Light–perception
coupling_families.why: Light is physically required for ordinary vision and symbolically associated with knowledge in many traditions.

coupling_families.name: Dark–unknown
coupling_families.why: Darkness can function as a metaphor for what is unseen; it should not be treated as intrinsically evil.

coupling_families.name: Heaven–earth
coupling_families.why: Vertical cosmology provides the project's upper/lower vocabulary.

coupling_families.name: Above–below
coupling_families.why: The same axis can encode physical position and project symbolism.

coupling_families.name: Root–crown
coupling_families.why: Plant architecture couples below-ground anchoring with above-ground growth.

coupling_families.name: Crown–throne
coupling_families.why: Crown and throne can be compared as images of culmination and authority, while keeping their traditions distinct.

coupling_families.name: Canopy–house
coupling_families.why: A canopy physically provides habitat and symbolically resembles shelter.

coupling_families.name: Forest–network
coupling_families.why: Plant-fungal networks create real biological interactions that enrich the project's network metaphor.

coupling_families.name: Soil–microbiome
coupling_families.why: Plant growth depends on complex soil biological and chemical processes.

coupling_families.name: Potato–agriculture
coupling_families.why: The symbolic object is also a major agricultural commodity and food crop.

coupling_families.name: Food–value
coupling_families.why: The potato crosses biological, nutritional, household, agricultural and commodity layers.

coupling_families.name: Commodity–network
coupling_families.why: A physical crop becomes a chain of economic relationships.

coupling_families.name: Value-chain–tree
coupling_families.why: Supply chains can be visualized as branching flows, while actual supply networks usually contain loops and multiple suppliers.

coupling_families.name: North–network
coupling_families.why: The North Programme treats geography as a network of relationships rather than a fixed boundary.

research_queue: Complete a source-backed potato biology profile including tuber anatomy, eyes, dormancy, sprouting, disease, storage and cultivars.
Expand thalamus records from the generic thalamus into major nuclei and pathways with source-backed functions.
Map biblical house/room/door/tree/vine/ladder passages by book, chapter, verse, genre and interpretive tradition.
Map comparative tree, mountain, axis, eye, vessel and threshold motifs across traditions without collapsing them into one religion.
Add geometry calculations for vesica dimensions, intersection area, triangle construction and transformations.
Add graph-theory records for tree, DAG, cyclic graph, bipartite graph, hub-and-spoke, lattice and flow network.
Connect every country to at least one economic, demographic, energy, infrastructure and geopolitical relationship where data permits.
Expand energy records into production, generation, transmission, storage, imports, exports and interconnectors.
Expand technology into supply chains: semiconductor → equipment → materials → fabrication → packaging → cloud/data centres.
Expand security records into legal mandate → jurisdiction → oversight → agency → event relationships.
Expand religion records into tradition → text → institution → ritual → geography → historical transformation.
Audit every isolated node and decide whether it needs an edge, a parent, a source or an explicit isolation reason.
Audit every relationship target and create missing canonical nodes or explicit external-reference semantics.
Audit frontend routes so every important canonical node has a reachable page.
Audit duplicate lexicons and cosmology files and create aliases rather than competing canonical definitions.
Make the Atlas able to show why two records are coupled, what evidence supports the coupling, and what remains interpretation.
quality_rules: Every meaningful major record gets relationship edges
Every empirical claim gets attributable evidence
Every mythic interpretation is marked as such
Every cross-domain analogy states its boundary
